neighbours.label: a lowercase rank or institution noun that stands alone for one particular holder: 'the king', 'the duke', 'the prince', 'the cathedral'; quiet when the same word is a capitalised part of a name (King Henry)
fire: When the envoys arrived at court, the king kept them waiting for three days.
Later that year the duke granted the town a charter to hold a weekly fair.
The petition was carried to London and laid before the king in person.
Two knights rode ahead to warn the prince that the bridge had fallen.
By the time the harvest was in, the duke had already sold the estate.
The monks sent word to the king that the abbey could pay no more.
Pilgrims crossed the square and went into the cathedral to hear the choir.
In return for the loan, the king gave the merchants the right to trade in wool.
quiet: When the envoys arrived at court, King Edward kept them waiting for three days.
Later that year Duke William granted the town a charter to hold a weekly fair.
The petition was carried to London and laid before Parliament in person.
Two knights rode ahead to warn Prince Rupert that the bridge had fallen.
By the time the harvest was in, the miller had already sold the grain.
The monks sent word to their brothers that the abbey could pay no more.
Pilgrims crossed the square and went into the tavern to hear the fiddler.
In return for the loan, the merchants gave the weavers the right to trade in wool.

notes: Card: peak ' king' x10, then ' university', ' fort', ' president', ' saint', 'ica' (basil|ica), ' duke', ' Prince'. Probes: 'waited for the duke' 0.55, 'the king refused' 0.39, 'the bishop at the cathedral' 0.31, 'to the university' 0.18; 'King Henry refused' 0.01, 'the farmer' 0.11, 'the cook' 0.11.
